observations: README.md is part of the shipped allow-list, so a documentation rewrite is a release-content change: it invalidates the pin and both pieces of acceptance evidence until they are regenerated.

The host acceptance is cheap enough (about 4 minutes for both hosts in parallel on this machine) that re-running it after each documentation correction was preferable to shipping a pin whose evidence described different bytes.

The two review rounds found 17 claims that no amount of self-review had caught; the failing classes were behavioural absolute statements ("always", "never", "only when") about code paths the docs summarised rather than read line by line.
remainingRisksAndUnverified: The release bytes are fixed by the committed release/ tarball rather than rebuilt by CI (deliberate; see RELEASE.md section 1). pack:check, release:verify and test/release-pin.test.mjs make a silent drift impossible, but only if the tarball and the pin are changed together.

The v0.2.0-rc.1 tag still disagrees with the bytes published on its Release (fc41f0e0... vs the d24f5e52... pinned by that tag). Fixing it needs a tag move or an asset overwrite, both out of scope here; the hardened workflow now fails loudly on that shape.
The guard remains a heuristic policy check, not a shell/JavaScript sandbox. Promoted host code runs cooperatively and needs trusted approval.

The path that manually disposes the underlying bundle Fiber is still not covered: disposeTrial goes through the official runner stop/undefine, and a manual probe cannot assert on itself. It is not a documented user shutdown path.

The domain evaluator stays advisory: promotionGates is the production authority and the evaluator contributes a regression veto, but no host-provided independent production baseline/test metric is wired in yet.
continuous/ and governance/ are unit-tested pure domain modules and are not reached by the orchestrator runtime loop, so the host acceptance does not protect them.

Internal and undocumented host surfaces are still read (ctx.events._hooks, ctx.reflect._getImpl(), Include EntryTree/Entry internals). runtime.internal-api probes each one and degrades to `degraded` when missing, but every DSH upgrade still requires a full re-acceptance.
External drift that persists during a Trial is still refused rather than reconciled: the recovery signature is a before/after observable inventory and the baseline is never rebuilt.
event-bridge.key has no rotation or revocation procedure; it is created once in the data root and disable/uninstall leave it in place.
The file-backed failure memory remains last-writer-wins and save() does not fsync; the cross-process lock protects the domain archive transaction, not that file.
Metric IDs are not an authorization boundary.
No npm publication, code signing, provenance attestation (SLSA) or SBOM.
The npm dist-tag for 0.2.1-alpha.1 moves; the acceptance records that exact version, not the tag.

Documented in this release and not fixed: the autonomous observer mode/unattended values are not a precondition for starting an isolated Trial, and an unrecognised promotion journal phase is rolled back and removed by startup recovery while the doctor reports blocked with no repair.
Not verified here: Code Scanning alert history beyond "this analysis succeeded with no open alerts for this commit", and any behaviour of DSH hosts outside the two declared, re-accepted versions.
